questions: Do you have any close blood relatives with a similar movement disorder or dystonia?
Did these abnormal postures first appear before the age of 20?
Are you currently taking any medications, particularly antipsychotics, metoclopramide, or antimalarials?
Do the spasms get noticeably worse as the day progresses and improve after sleep?
Did you have any problems during birth, or were you slow to reach developmental milestones as a child?
Have you ever been diagnosed with liver disease, jaundice, or Wilson's disease?
Do you also experience slowness of movement, stiffness, or a resting tremor of the hands?
Have you noticed any problems with your memory, thinking, or mood changes?
Does lightly touching the affected body part, or performing a specific gesture, temporarily reduce the muscle spasms?
Did the abnormal posture begin in one hand or foot and gradually spread to other parts of the body?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: GM1 gangliosidosis type III due to biallelic pathogenic GLB1 variants (β-galactosidase deficiency)

1. Wilson disease – excluded by normal serum caeruloplasmin/copper and 24-hour urinary copper, though would warrant slit-lamp Kayser–Fleischer examination if not already performed
2. Early-onset primary torsion dystonia (e.g., DYT1) – not excluded genetically as the panel finding may not have covered TOR1A, but the bilateral putaminal signal change and GLB1 result are against it
3. Pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN) – usually shows the "eye of the tiger" globus pallidus sign rather than the putaminal pattern seen here, and would not explain biallelic GLB1 variants
